text: Every developer on the team needs dbt to connect to Snowflake, with real credentials, without ever committing a secret to the repo. This lesson writes that connection file for a team, not just one solo developer.

profiles.yml lives at a developer's own home folder, never inside the project repo. This platform defines two targets, dev and prod, same shape, each pointing at a different schema, with every credential read through env_var instead of written as literal text.
Target dev is the default. Running plain dbt build with no target flag builds into the safe dev schema automatically — touching prod by hand requires a deliberate, explicit dbt build --target prod.

Both targets use the transformer role and the transforming warehouse Lesson 3 built specifically for dbt. Running dbt debug after writing this file confirms the account, user, role, warehouse, and database all actually resolve.

A real team takes this one step further, giving each developer a personal dev schema so builds never collide. Snowflake's foundation is now in place — Chapter 3 starts building the actual dbt model layer on top of it.
